events.title: The execution of Girolamo Savonarola
events.shortBlurb: The Dominican preacher who had ruled Florence with calls to repentance was hanged and burned in its great square…
body: On 23 May 1498 the Dominican friar Girolamo Savonarola was executed in the Piazza della Signoria at Florence, together with two of his brethren. A fiery preacher of repentance and reform, he had for a time held great sway over the city after the fall of the Medici, denouncing corruption and urging a stricter Christian life.

His attacks on abuses reached the papal court, and he was excommunicated by Pope Alexander VI and at last condemned by both civil and ecclesiastical authorities. He was hanged and his body burned, his ashes cast into the Arno. His memory has remained disputed ever since — reformer and prophet to some, rebel to others — and he was never canonized.
